title: Smash the Two Heaviest Stones

concept.title: A max-heap answers "which is the biggest now?" again and again
body: Some processes repeat the same step: *take the largest element, do something, and put a new element back*. After every step the largest element can be a different one, so sorting once is not enough, and sorting after each step costs O(n log n) every time. A **max-heap** keeps the largest element on top, and both taking it and inserting a new element cost only O(log n).

Here the step is: take the two heaviest stones; if their weights are equal, both are destroyed; otherwise the lighter one is destroyed and the heavier one loses the weight of the lighter one (the stone `x - y` goes back into the heap).

body.code:
import heapq
heap = [-x for x in stones]           # heapq is a min-heap: negate to get a max-heap
heapq.heapify(heap)
while len(heap) > 1:
    first = -heapq.heappop(heap)
    second = -heapq.heappop(heap)
    if first != second:
        heapq.heappush(heap, -(first - second))
print(-heap[0] if heap else 0)

body: There are at most `n - 1` steps (each step removes at least one stone), so the whole simulation takes O(n log n).

statement: There are `n` stones with the given weights. In every step take the two heaviest stones with weights `x >= y`. If `x == y` both stones are destroyed. Otherwise the stone with weight `y` is destroyed and the other one gets the weight `x - y`. Repeat until at most one stone is left. Print the weight of the last stone, or 0 if no stone is left.
inputFormat: The second line has `n` numbers: the weights of the stones.
outputFormat: Print the weight of the last stone, or 0.

examples.note: 8 and 7 become 1; 4 and 2 become 2; 2 and 1 become 1; 1 and 1 are both destroyed; one stone of weight 1 is left.

hints: After each step the heaviest stones may be different ones: use a max-heap.
Take two stones from the heap; if their weights differ, put the difference back.
When fewer than two stones remain, print the remaining weight or 0.

explanation: A max-heap gives the two heaviest stones in each step; if their weights differ, the difference is pushed back. The loop ends when at most one stone remains.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

import heapq
heap = [-x for x in a]
heapq.heapify(heap)
while len(heap) > 1:
    first = -heapq.heappop(heap)
    second = -heapq.heappop(heap)
    if first != second:
        heapq.heappush(heap, -(first - second))
print(-heap[0] if heap else 0)
